clue.text: Vehicle holds up progress? Not true!

indicators.note: the vehicle word holds the other piece, so it wraps around it

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for progress is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to go is to make progress

explanation.surface: A slow vehicle is blocking the traffic, and someone protests at a false claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GO into OG, and 'holds' puts OG inside BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false or fake is said to be phoney, sham, not genuine.

clue.text: Dog dropped tail to receive fuss

indicators.note: the dog's name loses its final letter, as if its tail were docked

parts.note: Fido is a stock name for a pet dog
to get something is to receive it

explanation.surface: A dog whose tail has been docked is getting a lot of attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped tail' takes the O off FIDO, leaving FID.
explanation.definitionFit: To fidget is to fuss restlessly with the hands or move about.

clue.text: Announced a number have cleared out

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a crowd has left the building.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something is to state it formally or make it known publicly.

clue.text: Airport's uplifting quotation on a burning issue

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplifting means the word for quotation is lifted up, read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a short familiar quotation or saying
a wick is what burns in a candle, playfully an issue that is on fire

explanation.surface: A rousing quotation on an urgent public controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns TAG into GAT. 'burning issue' looks like a hot topic but means the candle's wick; Gatwick is London's second airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatwick is the major international airport south of London.

clue.text: Fear of redundancy drove them to breaking point

definitions.text: Fear of redundancy drove them to breaking point

parts.words: Fear of redundancy drove them to breaking point
parts.note: reads as stressed workers reaching their limit, but means early nineteenth-century textile workers who smashed the new machines they feared would put them out of work

explanation.surface: Workers afraid of losing their jobs are pushed to the edge of collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking point' is literal: the Luddites broke machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were English weavers who wrecked mechanised looms that threatened their livelihoods.

clue.text: Banked left

definitions.meaning: put money into a bank account
set down or placed somewhere and abandoned

explanation.definitionFit: Money is deposited in a bank, and a thing set down and left is deposited.

clue.text: Cop in male form

indicators.note: form means the letters are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A policeman described as a cop in the shape of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges COP, IN and MALE; the whole clue also describes a male officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop is a slang word for a male police officer.

clue.text: Well salted

definitions.meaning: preserved with salt, like bacon or fish

explanation.definitionFit: A patient restored to health is cured, and meat preserved by salting is cured.

clue.text: Record is within a couple of figures

indicators.note: within places the little word inside the other piece

parts.note: D and C are two Roman numerals, 500 and 100

explanation.surface: A sales record set by a narrow margin of a couple of figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A gramophone record is a disc.

clue.text: Stop in front of a humble dwelling

indicators.note: in front of places the first piece before the rest

parts.note: a bung is a stopper for a hole
low means modest or humble in rank

explanation.surface: A halt outside a modest home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: People enter for this sort of sport

definitions.text: People enter for this sort of sport

parts.words: People enter for this sort of sport
parts.note: reads as people signing up for a competition, but means sport played after going in through a door, under a roof

explanation.surface: Competitors sign up for a particular kind of game.
explanation.definitionFit: An indoor sport is one played inside a building rather than out of doors.

clue.text: Can make a move

definitions.meaning: to begin moving or bestir oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for jail, like can; to stir is also to start moving.

clue.text: Bird dog gets drunk

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
to dog someone is to follow them, to tail them

explanation.surface: A pet bird and a dog share a booze-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is the past participle used as a noun: something drunk, a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixed alcoholic drink, a thing that is drunk.

clue.text: Overtime pay for a barman

parts.note: reads as extra wages for a pub worker, but the man of the bar is a barrister, paid an extra daily fee when a case runs on

explanation.surface: A pub worker claims extra wages for working late.
explanation.walkthrough: A barman here is a member of the Bar, a barrister.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is the extra fee paid to counsel for each further day a trial lasts.

clue.text: Kind of resort where disease is treated

indicators.note: treated means the letters are worked on and processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A health resort where illness is cured.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort is a holiday town on the coast.

clue.text: Ratification contains error

indicators.note: error suggests the letters have gone wrong and come out jumbled

explanation.surface: An official approval document turns out to include a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is official approval or confirmation of a measure.

clue.text: Local draughtsman?

parts.note: reads as a nearby technical artist, but means the person in a pub who draws draught beer

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood technical drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British word for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster draws beer from the tap for customers in an inn.

clue.text: A city set within a river

indicators.note: within places the word for set inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
laid means set down or placed

explanation.surface: A city built on the banks of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts LAID inside DEE, giving DELAIDE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Actor needs new suit a month

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in a different order

parts.note: Nov is the short form of November

explanation.surface: A performer requires a fresh costume every month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SUIT into USTI. Peter Ustinov was a British actor and writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Peter Ustinov was an Oscar-winning stage and film performer.

clue.text: A royal person in Canadian capital surrounded by a crowd

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first pieces are enclosed by the word for crowd

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the capital letter of Canadian is C

explanation.surface: A royal visitor in Ottawa is mobbed by onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canadian capital' is not Ottawa but the initial C; 'surrounded by' puts IN plus C inside PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a female member of a royal family.

clue.text: Still in uniform

definitions.meaning: yet more, as in still better

explanation.definitionFit: Even better means still better, and an even surface is uniform.

clue.text: The girl who took me back to mother

indicators.note: took back means the word me is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A girl who brought someone home to meet her mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a common girl's name.

clue.text: A way of acting part of Hamlet's madness

definitions.meaning: the naturalistic acting technique of Stanislavski and the Actors Studio
Polonius says of Hamlet: though this be madness

explanation.definitionFit: Method acting is a performance technique, and Polonius found method in the prince's apparent lunacy.

clue.text: Bandmaster so attached 0 to his country

parts.note: the bandmaster was American, so his country is the USA

explanation.surface: A bandleader so devoted to his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: John Philip Sousa was the American composer of military marches, so 'his country' is the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sousa led the US Marine Band and wrote marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.

clue.text: Repeatedly set about a fly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the piece is used twice over
about means the letters are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps setting about swatting a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SET into TSE, and 'Repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Idleness in battle

definitions.meaning: fighting, engaged in combat, as a phrase in two words

explanation.definitionFit: Lack of activity is idleness, and soldiers fighting are said to be in action.

clue.text: The spirit of my French translation

parts.note: de is the French for of
mon is the French for my

explanation.surface: A ghost recalled from a French version of my book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French translation' applies to both words: of my becomes DE MON.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil spirit.

clue.text: Way home from the inn

parts.note: a road is a way
a house is a home

explanation.surface: Walking back to one's house after leaving the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadhouse is an inn or bar on a main road outside town.
